answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to post a refundable bond before it can submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm fabricated identities or coordinated self-dealing. Auditors sample tasks unpredictably and compare claimed contributions across accounts, while a trellis of reputation links raises scrutiny for clusters sharing funding or behavior. The oasis of easy account creation remains, but a zephyr of fake profiles now risks losing real capital and accumulated reputation, making large-scale Sybil attacks costly rather than merely tedious.
